title: Drama dissertation
titleCn: 戏剧论文与《贝奥武夫》排演讨论

paragraphs.text: Now, Lee, I need to speak with you about your drama dissertation. I've noted a few errors.
I'm sorry to hear that. What can I improve?
Have you thought about including some historical content, as history has a great bearing on how we perceive drama today?
I understand that, but it's difficult to capture a moment in history to put it on screen in a way that's true to the era. So I decided to omit that line of reasoning altogether.

That's fair. My greatest concern is that your dissertation may cause a potential political risk. The way you've conveyed your overall theme may not sit well with some readers. It's somewhat inappropriate.
I'll try to amend that.

I understand you're using the example of the play Beowulf throughout your dissertation. There is a scene which depicts the assassination of a tyrant. Do you feel that this is too graphic and perhaps not suitable for modern audiences?
I think it suits the attitude of the play quite well. It's a long play, and that scene is integral. But I do believe that the main character is too rigid. He needs to lighten up a little.
I agree with you. The play is not written to lend scope to his character. I've made a comment in the margin on your paper regarding the historical use of the Greek chorus, which may help you.
Thank you.
As research for your dissertation, I believe you will be directing the play Beowulf to be acted by our first-year drama students. How is it progressing?
It's going well. I've had some difficulty getting the music right. There is some jazz music at the beginning, which I think will appeal to younger audiences.
I feel it would be more appropriate historically to use classical music throughout, given that this isn't a modern play.

I had wanted to go for a more modern adaptation, but I see you are right. So I'll make the changes. I'm having some trouble with the costumes and makeup. So far, I've given the characters heavy makeup and jewelry that will show more prominently in the low lighting. What would you advise?

As far as costumes are concerned, it's advisable not to use too much black. It makes it difficult to differentiate between characters. I noticed some of your characters are brightly dressed, which I approve, and there should be an obvious distinction between the male and female characters.
Okay, got it.
How do you feel about the lighting? Often, the use of bright and dark lighting can be used for emphasis.
The females will wear eyeshadow to differentiate, as there should be a big distinction between the principal actor and the supporting roles.
I prefer the main character to be more pronounced. He will have a spotlight directly on him to reinforce his role.
The lighting man will be busy, but it will make a change from him mainly lighting the stage. Here's a rough map of the stage area. Can you walk me through your layout?
Okay. There will be many costume changes. So to facilitate this, I've placed a mirror here right beside the door.
Excellent. What are the columns for?
To attract the audience's attention, I've placed columns in the middle to lend a sense of power to the production. This will also be in keeping with the setting.
How will you create the backdrops?
Because we can't replicate all the backdrops required for the play, I've set up a screen right at the back to project them as a video display. I think the effect will be quite striking.
I like your inventiveness.
To create the dramatic backdrop I'm hoping for, on the right side in the corner, I'll place a huge archway, which will be used in several scenes.
Ah, I understand you are using the traditional Greek method of a chorus.
Yes. Here in front of the stage, there will be a box on which the chorus will stand to speak directly to the audience regarding scene changes.
Excellent. Email me if you need any assistance.
Thanks.
